pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The experimental `unstable_Activity` element now has its own `react.activity` identity and reconciler work tag instead of being exported as the Offscreen type. Client reconciliation represents it as an Activity fiber wrapping an Offscreen child, server rendering sends it through the existing Offscreen path, and naming/DevTools logic recognizes it as `Activity`.

behavior_changes.description: Callers importing `unstable_Activity` now receive the distinct global symbol `react.activity`, rather than the Offscreen element type. Identity comparisons and element construction using this export therefore distinguish Activity from Offscreen.
evidence: A new `react.activity` symbol is defined and exported from ReactClient as `unstable_Activity`.

behavior_changes.description: The client reconciler now accepts Activity as an element type, creates a dedicated Activity work item, and reconciles its children through an Offscreen child carrying the Activity `mode` and `children` properties.
evidence: Fiber creation dispatches Activity elements to a dedicated factory.
Activity begin-work constructs Offscreen props from the supplied mode and children.

behavior_changes.description: During server rendering, Activity elements are handled by the same rendering path as Offscreen elements.
evidence: The Activity and Offscreen symbol cases share the call to `renderOffscreen`.

behavior_changes.description: Fiber naming and DevTools inspection can now present the dedicated work tag as `Activity`, rather than treating the exported component solely as Offscreen.
evidence: The reconciler name resolver and DevTools display-name logic return `Activity` for the new tag.
The current DevTools work-tag map assigns Activity tag 31.

local_risks.description: Code built around the previous experimental identity may no longer recognize `unstable_Activity` as Offscreen. Consumers comparing element types or constructing protocol values directly need migration or compatibility coverage because Activity and Offscreen are now separate global symbols.

Client and server use different internal representations: the client introduces an Activity wrapper around Offscreen behavior, while the server dispatches Activity directly to `renderOffscreen`. A reviewer should verify that this preserves mode, ref, hydration, and tree-shape invariants rather than producing client/server semantic drift.

The numeric work tag is effectively shared protocol data between the reconciler and DevTools. Future changes must keep tag 31 synchronized across these packages and preserve the version mapping, or inspection could misclassify fibers.
